text: Unlike Heron-6, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Kestrel-3 is 5097. Nobody should assume the port of Kestrel-3 applies to Heron-6, the port differs.
Pages from Siskin-8 land on the pager rotation of Mateo Whitlock before anyone else.
The primary datacenter of Kestrel-3 is Osaka; failover is handled by operations.
For Heron-6 the port is 9662. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
The retirement date for Godwit-9 is July 28, 2027; after that day it stops serving.
For Lark-9 the port is 9823. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Unlike Kestrel-3, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Siskin-8 is 7756. Nobody should assume the port of Siskin-8 applies to Kestrel-3, the port differs.
The yearly budget for Godwit-9 is $2225k, covering licences and hosting.
The owner of Heron-6 is the Quill team, and every change to Heron-6 goes through their review. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The owner of Lark-9 is the Ledger team, and every change to Lark-9 goes through their review.
Pages from Kestrel-3 land on the pager rotation of Kenji Zielinski before anyone else.
Godwit-9 has one owner, the Tessera team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The yearly budget for Kestrel-3 is $1995k, covering licences and hosting. An older draft of this note was archived.
Swift-9 reaches its retirement date on February 18, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
Siskin-8 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling.
Heron-6 runs in the Cairo datacenter, next to its database.

Unlike Kestrel-3, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Heron-6 is Nadia Whitlock. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Heron-6 applies to Kestrel-3, the pager rotation differs.
The owner of Siskin-8 is the Prism team, and every change to Siskin-8 goes through their review.
The rate limit of Godwit-9 is 2400 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Swift-9 is implemented in Rust; the language was chosen for its tooling.
Finance fixed the budget of Swift-9 at $2465k, reviewed every quarter.
Unlike Siskin-8, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Lark-9 is Go. Nobody should assume the language of Lark-9 applies to Siskin-8, the language differs.
Unlike Heron-6, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Swift-9 is the Lattice team. Nobody should assume the owner of Swift-9 applies to Heron-6, the owner differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Lark-9 at $4075k, reviewed every quarter. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Unlike Kestrel-3, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Heron-6 is $1280k. Nobody should assume the budget of Heron-6 applies to Kestrel-3, the budget differs.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Lark-9, which is 350 requests per minute.
Swift-9 enforces a rate limit of 3200 requests per minute per caller. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Swift-9, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Siskin-8 is 3100 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Siskin-8 applies to Swift-9, the rate limit differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Heron-6, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Godwit-9 is the Tallinn datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Godwit-9 applies to Heron-6, the datacenter differs.
Plan around the retirement date of Kestrel-3: April 27, 2028 is when it goes dark. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
